articles.title: Héctor Rodas: “ Si alcanzamos la permanencia este año, estaremos cerca del 1:1”
articles.standfirst: El director deportivo del Levante confirma la llamada del Valencia en el último día de mercado por Etta Eyong
articles.summary: El director deportivo del Levante confirma la llamada del Valencia en el último día de mercado por Etta Eyong
articles.body: El director deportivo, Héctor Rodas, ha comparecido este mediodía en la sala de prensa del estadio Ciutat de Valencia tras el cierre del mercado de fichajes de verano para valorar las diferentes operaciones del Levante. “Ha sido un mercado muy intenso y hemos hecho muchas cosas. Dar las gracias a todo mi equipo y Danvila por el esfuerzo económico para hacer una plantilla competitiva. Ha sido un mercado muy complicado. Hemos empezado con un fair play de cinco millones que es muy complicado. hemos tenido que ser ingeniosos para hacer buscar una estabilidad y empezar nuevos procesos como la ciudad deportiva. Estoy muy satisfecho y contento del mercado. Hemos tenido un final bonito” “Etta es un gran activo. Hizo un inicio de temporada que llamó la atención, aunque después de la copa África resurgido Carlos Espí. Siempre que ha participado atenido muy buena actuación. Han llegado ofertas de diferentes clubes de países exóticos, premier, liga española…pero el jugador ha decidido quedarse e intentar sacar su mejor versión” “Tu imagínate que el club genera 100 millones de euros, pero la liga te dice que solo tienes 25 millones porque tienes que generar plusvalía. ¿Cómo consigues que esa cifra suba?, vendiendo jugadores, etc…el cómputo general nos ha permitido hacer una plantilla competitiva y gracias al esfuerzo económico de Danvila, hemos tenido un fair play digno. Vender por una cantidad de 40 millones de euros, no es fácil. Hemos recortado mucho de la herencia recibida” “Nosotros en las ultimas horas estábamos centrados en la inscripción de Petar Ratkov. Si hubiéramos tenido el saldo necesario para cerrarlo, lo hubiéramos hecho. Lo intentamos, desde enero estamos hablando pero le advertimos de nuestra situación” “Está traspasado a America. Tiene que solucionar algunas cosas con el equipo de destino. Cuando esté cerrado se hará oficial” “Nosotros tenemos que vender a nuestros activos y no es fácil traer las ofertas que hemos traído. Nosotros tratamos de mediar y él ha rechazado todas las propuestas.Para el club nos hubiera venido muy bien. Hubo una llamada del Valencia para preguntar por su situación, al igual que de otros equipos de Primera, pero tenemos que respetar su decisión. El Valencia pidió una información y ya no recibí ninguna llamada más” “Vamos a pelear por los que haga falta. En nuestra hoja de ruta contábamos en que no tenías saldo suficiente para poder hacer una operación. Tenemos a Cabello y a Toljan que pueden jugar en esa posición. Tenemos otras opciones si el mister decide que Manu Sánchez no debe jugar” “Yo estoy satisfecho igual. Yo creo que, con el Fair Play que tenemos y que estamos manejando, doblar dos jugadores por puestos, es complicado. Estoy muy satisfecho del trabajo, nos hemos sacrificado mucho” “El año pasado, al inicio de temporada, teníamos los mismo numero de delanteros que ahora. Queríamos un perfil de delantero como Carlos Espí. Llegamos mucho al área y queríamos un delantero con esas características” “Al final, por nuestra situación financiera, no podemos optar a por todo tipos de jugadores. Nosotros vendemos una ciudad espectacular y un ambiente impresionante y el míster aporta mucho. Luis consigue desarrollar muy bien a los jugadores y en ese cómputo, es muy importante” “La comparativa no sabría que decirte. Son perfiles diferentes y confío mucho en la plantilla de este año. Es verdad que, con Luís Castro desde el inicio, es un punto muy a favor. Partimos con esa cierta ventaja de que el míster ya conoce a la plantilla. No vivir con prisa y ansiedad por conocer a los jugadores y puntuar en cada partido, es muy importante” “Al final tengo documentos que demuestran que se hizo antes de las 12. La liga ha sido flexible en otros casos” “Teniendo fichas libres y teniendo algo de saldo, si existe alguna oportunidad, veremos si podemos hacer algo” “El primer año de Carlos en el Levante, rechazamos una oferta importante, aunque para luchar por el objetivo del ascenso, tenía que quedarse. América hizo una oferta muy grande y era una situación complicada, porque en pocos meses era agente libre. Hay muchas oportunidades pero al final surgió la oferta de México, que él vera con muy buenos ojos. Hay que recordarlo con buenos ojos porque nos ha dado mucho” “Hemos hecho la mejor plantilla con el presupuesto que teníamos. El entrenador está satisfecho. Aunque es verdad que no podemos decir que hemos hecho una buena plantilla, si al final no conseguimos el objetivo. Hemos hecho un gran esfuerzo y hemos hecho ventas muy complicadas” “Nosotros tenemos que ir a por talento joven. Este jugador lo seguimos durante mucho tiempo y en Youth League tenía mucho escaparate. Era un operación complicada porque aún tenía contrato. Queremos que sea un jugador de futuro y el mister lo ve cada día mucho mejor” “Pasamos una propuesta, aunque es cierto, que queremos que termine el mercado. A partir de ahora, iniciaremos diferentes operaciones con jugadores como Dela para que se pueda quedar nosotros durante muchos años” “Analizando la plantilla y, estando doblada la posición con Nacho Peréz y Toljan, el mister quería analizarlo. Hablamos con su entorno para decirle que lo mejor era buscarle una salida en forma de cesión. No nos hemos puesto de acuerdo al final y lo mejor es que salga del club” “Para hacer once fichajes hemos tenido que llamar a 50 jugadores. Como el año pasado con un portero que firmó por el Barça y se ha arrepentido. Este año la incertidumbre la marcaba el fair play. Hemos sido valientes pero la incertidumbre no lo llevamos muy bien. Nos gusta tenerlo todo controlado. Por suerte ha salido todo muy bien” “Confiamos mucho en nuestra cantero. Nos ha dado muchos frutos en los últimos años y queremos potenciarla. Queremos cuidarla lo máximo. Hemos hecho cambios en la Ciudad Deportiva de Buñol y en la residencia. Confiamos mucho en la cantera porque tiene que ser importante. En el caso de Marc, lo renovamos en marzo es un chico que siente el Levante como suyo. Queremos que el jugador juegue cada fin de semana y compita. Es lo mejor para su desarrollo” “Se debe a la incertidumbre del club. Hasta la última jornada no sabes donde estás, si en Primera o en Segunda. La gente sabe la situación que tenemos. Si fuera por mí, hubiéramos tenido a Espí, Arriaga o Carlos Espí. La situación del club es así. Tenemos que sanear al club de la mejor manera posible. Ahora mismo, no nos lo podemos permitir. Prioriza la necesidad que tiene el club” “Les diría que sigan creyendo y apoyando al equipo. Esta unión hacía años que no la veía. Yo veo a la gente que anima como nunca. El jugador lo nota. Puede ser muy importante, como el año pasado. Están todos para renovar un año más” “Viendo las alternativas que teníamos decimos ir a por otro tipo de perfil. Nosotros lo comunicamos. Él ha encontrado un destino como Málaga y le deseo lo mejor” “Si tuviese dinero hubiera comparo a los jugadores cedidos . Hasta que no tengamos la regla uno a uno, será así. No te da para más. Tienen un valor de mercado de 8 o 10 millones y un salario muy bajo. Dentro de nuestras posibilidades hay que caminar para que todos los jugadores que tengamos, tanto cedidos como en propiedad, busquen el equilibro” “Si este año logramos la permanencia, estamos más cerca del uno a uno. Tenemos penalizaciones del pasado en cualquier traspaso o un salario. Así se hace muy complicado” “El entorno no fue todo lo profesional que digamos. Yo soy virgen y no debo favores a nadie. Trabajamos con agencias y, en este caso, no volveremos a trabajar con ellos” “El año pasado lo pescamos y él, se lo tiene que ganar en el día a día. Es una apuesta del club, como Cabello. El Club confía en ellos, como yo en mi caso cuando era canterano. Sino tienes un bagaje hay que trabajar para ganarse el puesto” “En el mundial de Qatar lo destacamos. No pudimos acercarnos para nada. Era para conocerlo y valorarlo. Al igual que el delantero de Egipto del Barça también estaba allí. Pero conoces al entorno y cuando ya conoces al entorno, empieza a preguntar. Ivy hizo una buena pretemporada con el equipo y preguntamos su situación y surgió esta oportunidad. El mister se entrevistó con él y decidió venir al Levante, rechazando ofertas de otros equipos y pasases que pagaban más. No tiene cláusula de minutos y lo pueden repescar.

articles.title: Real Madrid summer signing wins over fans and teammates after just 161 minutes under Mourinho
articles.summary: Marc Cucurella did not have to wait long to make an impression at Real Madrid.The 28-year-old summer signing had to wait until the third matchday of the 2026...
articles.body:
Marc Cucurella did not have to wait long to make an impression at Real Madrid.

The 28-year-old summer signing had to wait until the third matchday of the 2026/27 La Liga season for his first start under Jose Mourinho.

However, by the time the final whistle was blown against Malaga, the Spanish full-back had already begun to establish himself as a popular figure within the dressing room and among the supporters.

Cucurella completed the full 90 minutes as Madrid secured a comfortable 4-0 victory over Malaga , following his second-half appearance in the 4-1 win against Real Sociedad.

Now, according to AS , the performance reinforced what had already been visible during his opening weeks at the club: Cucurella has arrived with the personality, intensity and reliability to fit into Mourinho's team.

The outlet mentions that Cucurella finished the Malaga match with 76 touches and 51 attempted passes, completing 46 of them for an 88.2% success rate.

He also created a scoring opportunity and was heavily involved defensively, making four tackles and recovering possession five times. He won an early aerial duel and blocked an opposition shot.

Notably, these statistics only tell part of the story.

The biggest reaction came from the stands, where Cucurella was applauded on several occasions.

His defensive work was also recognised by his teammates, who repeatedly acknowledged his contributions during the match.

As far as Mourinho is concerned, it is clear that the Portuguese manager wants his players to understand their defensive responsibilities, and Cucurella appears comfortable with the physical demands of that role.

He can defend against wingers, contribute in possession and still provide an attacking outlet from full-back.

That combination gives Mourinho a dependable option without requiring constant tactical adjustments.

A quick connection with the Madrid dressing room

Cucurella's adaptation has not been limited to what he does during matches.

Since arriving at Real Madrid, the defender has developed relationships within the squad and has regularly been seen joking with teammates during training.

His connection with Carlos Espi has been particularly noticeable, with the pair often together during warm-ups.

So far, Cucurella has played only 161 minutes across three appearances since joining Real Madrid, so it would be premature to make sweeping conclusions about his long-term role.

However, first impressions matter, and his have been difficult to improve upon.

articles.title: Lincoln Riley: 'I don't buy into the false narrative' surrounding the empty seats at USC's Week 0 win
articles.summary: There were more empty seats than fans at USC's win over San Jose State.
articles.body:
Lincoln Riley isn't going to get in a back-and-forth about the number of people who were at his team's Week 0 win.

USC beat San Jose State on Saturday to open the 2026 season in front of more empty seats than fans at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. It was over 90 degrees and sunny in LA and, well, you can imagine how tempting the beach and other water-related activities would be compared to sitting in the sun for a game where the Trojans were a five-touchdown favorite.

Pictures of those empty seats went viral, however, and even forced USC to issue a statement about the lack of attendance . Riley was asked about the topic during his Tuesday news conference and dismissed the debate.

"This is USC, right? People are going to pay attention," Riley said. "People are going to have an opinion. It's part of being a blue-blood school. I don't buy into the false narrative. I think that comes from a lot of people that don't follow our program. And most of those who have never set foot in the Coliseum. The reality is during my years here, attendance has gone up every single year. As has our play in the Coliseum, including running the table last year in front of a lot of epic atmospheres and I expect that to happen again this year."

There are plenty of opportunities for the Coliseum to be full later in the season with home games against No. 2 Oregon, No. 17 Washington and No. 1 Ohio State all within the span of a month in the middle of the season. If fans aren't showing up for those games, then a legitimate debate is there to be had about USC fan support.

And let's be real, there are going to be myriad programs across the country who may also have more empty seats than normal in Week 1. Thanks to a heat dome across the southeast, heat indexes will be over 100 degrees in many college cities and towns.

The high in Austin, is set to be 96 for Texas' 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff against Texas State and the highs will be well into the 90s in places like Athens, Georgia, Tuscaloosa, Alabama, and Knoxville, Tennessee. If fans want to watch from home or in the shade by a pool, instead of going to a game against an inferior opponent, can you really blame them?

articles.title: El Atlético se lleva a Beltrán por su cláusula
articles.standfirst: El joven central abandona Butarque tras crecer desde cadete en la cantera pepinera
articles.summary: El joven central abandona Butarque tras crecer desde cadete en la cantera pepinera
articles.body: Beltrán Auguste Paolucci ya no pertenece al Leganés. El Atlético de Madrid abonó el último día de mercado la cláusula de rescisión del central hispano-argentino de 19 años, superior al millón de euros, para hacerse con uno de los jóvenes con mayor proyección de la cantera pepinera. Beltrán firmará hasta 2031, por el Atlético. Una operación que no gustó en Butarque por la apuesta realizada por el futbolista y por producirse mediante el pago de su cláusula al final del mercado de fichajes. Eso sí, supone el mayor ingreso del Leganés por un canterano que no había debutado oficialmente con el primer equipo de su historia. Auguste llegó al club en edad cadete y la pasada temporada dio el salto al filial siendo todavía juvenil. Este verano realizó la pretemporada con Rubén Albés y entró en las convocatorias de las dos primeras jornadas ante Girona y Real Oviedo. El Leganés pierde así una apuesta de futuro, aunque recibe una importante cantidad por un futbolista de sólo 19 años.

articles.title: El abonado del Villarreal mantiene su fidelidad en una Cerámica que este año crece
articles.standfirst: El Villarreal volverá a superar los 19.000 fieles mientras que el aforo de su estadio asciende hasta los 23. 173espectadores
articles.summary: El Villarreal volverá a superar los 19.000 fieles mientras que el aforo de su estadio asciende hasta los 23. 173espectadores
articles.body: El Villarreal CF volverá a contar esta temporada con el respaldo de más de 19.000 abonados, una cifra que confirma la fidelidad de su afición y mantiene la tendencia registrada durante los últimos años, en los que el club ha rondado habitualmente los 20.000 carnés. Este dato cobra especial relevancia después de los cambios y trabajos realizados durante el verano con motivo de la remodelación del Estadio de la Cerámica. Las actuaciones han permitido mejorar diferentes aspectos del recinto, especialmente los accesos y las condiciones de seguridad. Además, el aumento de precios de los abonos no ha afectado de forma significativa al número de abonados. Además, las obras han permitido ampliar la capacidad del estadio, que pasa a tener un aforo de 23.173 espectadores. De esta manera, se recuperan parte de los asientos que no pudieron utilizarse durante la pasada temporada. El nuevo reparto del estadio contempla algo más de 21.000 localidades destinadas a la afición local y alrededor de 2.000 plazas para los seguidores visitantes. La pasada campaña, más de 600 asientos de la zona reservada a las aficiones rivales no estuvieron disponibles, una situación que ha quedado resuelta tras la remodelación, permitiendo utilizar nuevamente toda la grada. Este próximo sábado será el estreno del estadio amarillo en la presente temporada con la visita del Deportivo de La Coruña. Los castellonenses han disputado los tres primeros partidos del campeonato a domicilio a causa de las obras

articles.title: Sergio Martínez se estrena con el primer equipo
articles.standfirst: El medio recién fichado del Racing se ejercitó a las órdenes de José Mourinho
articles.summary: El medio recién fichado del Racing se ejercitó a las órdenes de José Mourinho
articles.body: Segundo entrenamiento del Real Madrid de cara a la vista al Betis en La Cartuja (viernes, 21.00 horas). La principal novedad fue la presencia en la sesión de Sergio Martínez, el centrocampista de 19 años fichado del Racing el pasado 31 de agosto. Sergio Martínez, por el que el Madrid pagó unos tres millones de euros, llega para incorporarse en principio al Castilla, aunque la intención es que se deje ver por las sesiones de la primera plantilla para que José Mourinho pueda estar pendiente de su evolución. Con contrato hasta 2023, ha sido la gran apuesta del club para el primer filial blanco. Por lo demás, Tchouameni, Asencio, Mendy, Militão, Rodrygo, Endrick y Thiago continúan con sus procesos de recuperación. No se prevén novedades en la lista de este jueves ante el Betis, a la que no debe llgar ninguno de los jugadores que siguen al margen del grupo.

articles.title: Everton's transfer deadline day debacle leaves owners facing fan mutiny
articles.summary: Everton's transfer deadline day debacle over Folarin Balogun leaves owners The Friedkin facing fan mutiny, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Everton 's shambolic end to the transfer window has resulted in open revolt from supporters that places fierce scrutiny on owners The Friedkin Group and chief executive Angus Kinnear.

The last straw for fans already infuriated by the controversial proposed sale of home-grown youngster Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest - the deal was eventually blocked by Everton 's board in the face of the toxic reaction from the fanbase - was the bungled final day before the window closed.

Folarin Balogun's proposed £40m move from AS Monaco descended into high farce in the early hours of Wednesday morning after the original deal was renegotiated when issues arose with his medical, ending with the United States striker deciding to walk away from Everton's Finch Farm training base without signing.

And all after Balogun, 25, and both clubs had signed the deal sheet allowing the move to be completed after Tuesday's 23.00 BST transfer deadline.

Everton had scheduled an 8am flight to bring Balogun to Merseyside, but he was unable to arrive until later in the day. Everton were also frustrated at a delay in receiving documents related to the deal from Monaco.

When the problem with his medical cropped up, it prompted Everton to pursue a loan deal for Manchester United 's Joshua Zirkzee, who was happy to sign but was not allowed to leave Old Trafford. A move was also made for Aston Villa 's Tammy Abraham but did not progress as the striker wished to remain at Villa Park.

After failing to sign an alternative, a deal was eventually agreed with Monaco, minutes before the deadline, which would have resulted in a smaller up-front payment and a series of triggered payments based on how he progressed. The player's personal terms were unchanged.

It was only then that the former Arsenal striker had his change of heart, leaving Finch Farm with Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro telling journalists at a news conference on Wednesday that Balogun was "not comfortable" with how Everton treated him during his medical.

Everton believe they supported Balogun throughout the process, while being open about the issues identified. The club also made clear to the player they would work with Monaco to explore a solution that could still enable the transfer to be completed.

To make matters worse, and to shed an even more unflattering light on the club's strategy and operation, it all came after hours after Everton had sanctioned striker Beto's £15.5m move to Fiorentina.

Events unfolded as Everton 's most creative player Iliman Ndiaye was completing his £65m move to Manchester City .

Everton could point to the fact Balogun took a personal decision they could not reverse, but the bigger question is why they took until the final day of the window to address glaring long-term issues?

Kinnear, in what must now be looked upon as an ill-fated recent interview with BBC Radio Merseyside, announced Everton 's squad was "in a good place", adding: "The challenge is we want to get the absolute best player we can in their position. Our metric is that by the close of the transfer window we have achieved that."

He also relayed the views of Everton 's American owners that they regarded missing out on Europe last season as "failure". It was an announcement manager David Moyes admitted came as a "surprise".

After the events of recent days, the word "failure" is being applied to the owners and chief executive, not Moyes. And there will be no hiding place for TFG and Kinnear should things now go wrong.

The "good place" Kinnear spoke about has eventually amounted to leaving Moyes with just one striker in the raw Thierno Barry and only 18 senior, outfield players, a parlous state of affairs for the 63-year-old Scot, who has at times found it hard to disguise his dissatisfaction with the extent of the summer's transfer business.

Everton may have re-signed Jack Grealish on loan, and finally solved a right-back problem stretching back years by signing Ashley Maitland-Niles from Lyon for £3m, but the over-riding verdict on the club's transfer window has to be one of huge embarrassment for TFG and Kinnear.

Even the search for a right-back, a problem from last summer and further back, was not smooth, with Maitland-Niles being officially announced shortly after midnight after a £9.4m deal for Fulham 's Kenny Tete was shelved when the Cottagers could not find a suitable replacement.

As well as only one striker in Barry, Everton 's squad now has just one recognised right-back in Maitland-Niles and one left-back in Vitaliy Mykolenko after youngster Adam Aznou was allowed to join Malaga on loan.

The last few days have seen one major PR catastrophe narrowly avoided by pulling out of the sale of 19-year-old Armstrong, arguably Everton 's most promising academy product since Wayne Rooney, only to walk straight into another, highly damaging one.

After the Carabao Cup second-round win at Preston North End, Moyes said: "I still think we have got a lot of work to do. We need more players. Our squad is not big enough and we need to get more quality in some areas if we can do."

Moyes' thoughts will be worth much more than a penny, should he choose to air them publicly, while fans' groups have wasted no time in expressing their undisguised anger, with a petition even set up calling for Kinnear's resignation.

"The Everton Fans' Forum" issued a lengthy statement featuring widescale criticism of the club, saying the Toffees' squad had been left "dangerously short" in key areas.

It added: "The conclusion of this summer's transfer window leaves Everton supporters with serious questions about the club's planning, recruitment and decision-making.

"This is not about demanding that Everton spend recklessly. Supporters understand the financial restrictions the club operates under. We are not demanding marquee signings simply for the sake of it.

"We are demanding competence, preparation and accountability."

And the influential group "The 1878s", volunteers who have created huge flags, banners and tifos to enhance the atmosphere at Everton 's new Hill Dickinson Stadium, and whose efforts were described as "unbelievable" by Moyes, has responded to deadline day in similar vein.

In a statement it said it is "standing down for the foreseeable future" in protest, saying: "Like the rest of our fanbase, we are utterly disappointed and disgusted with how this transfer window has gone, especially the end of it.

"Also for fans asking, just to reiterate - when we design flags, there are rules and regulations that we have to adhere to regarding the wording on our flags during displays, we are not allowed derogatory or offensive wording or images.

"If we were able to get a load of flags in the ground to show our feelings of discontent, disappointment and anger over this whole situation, believe us, we would, but this is something that simply wouldn't be allowed."

As well as the last-day signings of Grealish and Maitland-Niles, Everton did make other acquisitions during the window, bringing in PFA Championship Player of the Year Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough.

Christian Norgaard was signed from Arsenal - although the 32-year-old Dane is currently injured with no comeback date - as a replacement for departed veteran Idrissa Gueye.

Deals for young German Merlin Rohl and England Under-21 winger Tyrique George, on loan last season, were confirmed. Brennan Johnson arrived from Crystal Palace in a straight swap with Dwight McNeil.

All this, however, has been overshadowed by a transfer deadline day that ended as nothing short of a debacle. In reality, they have ended this transfer markedly weaker than when they started it.

Everton are yet to issue any public statement on the events that have led to such damning criticism, fan rebellion and a loss of credibility for owners TFG - but there are many fences to be mended.

If that can be done successfully remains to be seen.

articles.title: Will Illinois-Missouri football rivalry actually return in 2027?
articles.summary: Braggin’ Rights on the gridiron?
articles.body:
The wait continues to find out when and where the 2027 football matchup between Illinois and Missouri will take place. Josh Whitman told the press on July 25 that the location has yet to be discussed and needs to be addressed soon.

"Not today," Whitman said when asked about the location of the 2027 game.

Kansas City, Chicago, St. Louis, Nashville, or either Champaign or Columbia are realistic options for the first game of the series.

As of now, the 2028 game is scheduled to be played in Champaign, while the 2029 game will be in Columbia. A neutral-site game would make the most sense for the first game of the new series, unless the schools want to move everything up a season and play the 2029 matchup at a neutral site.

The Illinois vs. Mizzou game was played in St. Louis for six straight seasons, and the former Rams stadium is still there, making it an easy choice. St. Louis is roughly in the middle of both campuses and would mirror the annual basketball matchup that has been played in the city for more than five decades.

The lack of discussion regarding the location is not particularly encouraging, especially after the reduction in games that was announced in the summer of 2025.

Illinois and Missouri originally announced plans to renew the rivalry all the way back in 2017. The first game was set to be played Sept. 26, 2026 — just a few weeks from now. Those plans were changed when an eight-year series was announced in 2020 but reduced to six games in 2025.

The original agreement between the two schools was as follows:

Sept. 26, 2026 — Champaign, Ill. Sept. 18, 2027 — Columbia, Mo. Sept. 16, 2028 — Champaign, Ill. Sept. 15, 2029 — Columbia, Mo. Sept. 18, 2032 — Champaign, Ill. Sept. 17, 2033 — Columbia, Mo. Sept. 16, 2034 — Champaign, Ill. Sept. 15, 2035 — Columbia, Mo.

The new agreement made last summer reduced the series from eight games to six, canceling the 2026 and 2032 matchups. The cancellation was agreed to by both sides and was largely due to both teams already having a power-conference opponent on their non-conference schedules for those seasons. The Illini have Duke at home in 2026, while the Tigers have Kansas on the docket for both 2026 and 2032.

The new contract between Illinois and Missouri looks similar:

2027 (Date TBD) — Site TBD Sept. 16, 2028 — Champaign, Ill. Sept. 15, 2029 — Columbia, Mo. 2033 (Date TBD) — Site TBD Sept. 16, 2034 — Champaign, Ill. Sept. 15, 2035 — Columbia, Mo.

Neither team has a Power Four opponent already scheduled during these six seasons, so it would be great to see this rivalry return in any form possible. Missouri has historically dominated Illinois and leads the all-time series 17-7, but the Illini have gotten much better in recent years.

This series would be great for the fans and great for college football, giving the sport a high-level matchup early in the season. The SEC is now required to play a Power Four opponent during non-conference play every season, while the Big Ten has yet to enforce a similar rule.There is no reason for Missouri to back out of this series with that rule coming into effect, so hopefully Illinois keeps its word and plays the game in 2027.

There is no need to panic yet, but hopefully we learn more about the location of the 2027 game — and the future of the series as a whole — over the next few months.

articles.title: Premier League transfer window: Sky Sports reporters rank your club's summer after dramatic Deadline Day
articles.summary: Sky Sports reporters rank and analyse every Premier League club's summer transfer window; top-flight clubs smashed their spending record, splashing £3.48bn on new signings
articles.body:
Eight is the number of senior players out and that's why I give Arsenal's summer business eight out of 10.

Gabriel Jesus , Gabriel Martinelli , Leandro Trossard , Christian Norgaard , Fabio Viera , Ethan Nwaneri (loan), Jakob Kiwior and Reiss Nelson are all out of the building, with the exception of Nwaneri - who still has a big future at the club - deemed surplus to requirements.

Cash in - over £100m - and wages saved. In Jesus' case, big wages.

If the club had secured a left winger to replace the two they sold, I'd have given nine out of 10. Either Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez coming in and it would have been a perfect 10. In the end, it wasn't to be.

Securing either was always a long shot but Arsenal deserve credit for even being in the conversation.

Fans are disappointed those two didn't come to the Emirates. But they accept it and understand.

Many, though, don't accept or understand why last season's two main left-sided attackers haven't been fully replaced. The club would have if they could have. But the right fit never emerged after the Vinicius saga.

So it's make do on the left. And the hierarchy, like Mikel Arteta , believe there's enough in the squad to do that. Newcomer Christos Tzolis , if a bit shaky last time out at Villa Park, has done well. The fans already love him.

Eberechi Eze has shown he can be impressive there as well. Also, Noni Madueke and Bukayo Saka can both do a job on the left if required.

In fact, playing one of them there is another way of giving Max Dowman more minutes. He could play down the right.

There's even a school of thought that Riccardo Calafiori could push further up the pitch. Remember Arteta finding new, unexpected roles for Mikel Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly ?

So, no new left winger. And no new striker. But Arteta has more options everywhere else.

One look at the bench at Villa Park underlines that. Injuries allowing, Arsenal have quality depth in defence and midfield.

Total personnel changes from game to game in those areas are now possible, with little drop-off in competitiveness.

It's been a good window for Arsenal. The ones Arteta really wanted were Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa . And he got them.

When Aston Villa lifted the Europa League no one would have imagined six of the starting line-up would be departing just weeks later - least of all Unai Emery .

How do you replace Morgan Rogers , Youri Tielemans , Ollie Watkins , Emiliano Martinez , Lucas Digne, and Ezri Konsa while staying within the financial rules tightly governing the club?

The answer has been to rebuild with younger, exciting players full of potential like Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, plus some experienced heads like Leon Goretzka and Aaron Wan-Bissaka . Nicolas Jackson won't need to adapt to the league and did well on his debut on Monday night.

Zion Suzuki also made a positive first showing in goal. Taylor Harwood-Bellis says he still has plenty to improve on but is convinced the manager can help him thrive at the top level.

That Unai Emery factor has to be taken into account along with how well the club have balanced the books this summer in the face of an unwanted rebuild.

So I'm optimistic about this summer's business - with the caveat that we need real evidence of what these players can do in a Villa shirt.

Bournemouth's summer contrasted with the summer of 2025, when they sold a number of key players. This summer was about keeping their best players - and they absolutely passed the test.

Rayan , Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott all remain at the club. Bournemouth have a model that allows players to move but they also want to ensure they have those players for a chunk of time.

Bournemouth also promised Marco Rose they wouldn't sell the team from beneath him. They wanted to give him the best chance to succeed, despite strong interest in all three players.

Being in Europe changes the dynamic of what Bournemouth can spend in order to meet UEFA's financial regulations. It was a real challenge because they had to add quality and depth while reducing costs.

Bournemouth's business looks really solid. They've added a goalkeeper - Michele Di Gregorio - who was the Juventus No 1 last season. They added a centre-back - Antonio Silva - who was linked with a number of big clubs not that long ago for what looks to be great value. Juanlu Sanchez looks to be a solid full-back, and Alvaro Rodriguez looks to bring something different in attack.

Bournemouth allowed fringe players to go and one of the other positives is they were decisive, acting early in the window. They were totally comfortable which meant that - for the first time in many years - they weren't doing business on Deadline Day.

Rose and the hierarchy will look back on this as a very successful summer - now they just have to deliver on the pitch.

I'm struggling to find a reason not to give Brentford top marks on their summer business. The priority was always to bring in a dependable midfielder they could build their future around. Enter Mamadou Sangare , whose £39m price tag is looking like a real bargain. Is it too early to say he's a candidate for signing of the season?

He's the biggest change to Brentford's starting XI but I'd wager late addition El Hadji Malick Diouf is likely to become a regular starter at left-back. Forward Jaidon Anthony has already started twice, Callum Wilson is proving why he's the perfect back-up (if not competitor) to Igor Thiago and centre-back Jannik Schuster provides cover, especially with Sepp van den Berg injured.

Plus, Brentford have managed to hold onto their key men. Jordan Henderson's leadership will be missed, but they've retained star attacking players Thiago, Kevin Schade and Yehor Yarmoliuk - someone who's really impressed bigger clubs recently - and tied down Michael Kayode and Vitaly Janelt with new contracts.

The only Deadline Day movement was the news that Jayden Meghoma went to Portsmouth on loan - a move in line with the club's determination to make sure their young players get game time.

I'm only avoiding giving Brentford a 10 because, as I'm sure Keith Andrews himself would say, there's always room for improvement!

It's been an uncharacteristically busy summer window for Brighton. The club have brought in nine players ready for the first team at a cost of nearly £170m. There is strength in depth in many areas - most notably in defence.

Luka Vuskovic came in for a club record £50m - something of a coup for the Seagulls. The arrival of young defensive midfielder Chema Andres from Stuttgart - a Spain U21 international - in a dramatic late twist on Deadline Day goes some way to filling the hole left by Carlos Baleba, who joined Manchester United.

He will need time to adapt to the Premier League but looks a real talent. They have lost a lot of experience and goal power in the shape of Danny Welbeck up front - they will be hoping loan signing Promise David can deliver on that front.

Liverpool target Yankuba Minteh is staying at the club. That should be considered significant for Brighton.

Once some of the injured players return and gel with the new signings, head coach Fabian Hurzeler will be hoping he has enough to successfully tackle the Premier League and Conference League.

Chelsea's squad has been revolutionised in this transfer window following a clear shift in strategy. Premier League-ready players have been brought in to complement the young, talented footballers already at the club. The pursuits of Jordan Henderson , Emiliano Martinez and Danny Welbeck marked a massive change from what we have seen from the club since the takeover.

Chelsea will continue to sign some of the best young players in world football, as seen with the arrival of Geovany Quenda . However, they have appreciated the need to bring in players who are ready to make an immediate impact.

They have also acted quickly to tie down Joao Pedro to an improved contract to ward off potential suitors. The core of this squad is here to stay.

Last season marked one of the worst in Chelsea's modern history. The campaign completely unravelled following Enzo Maresca's departure. The feeling was unsavoury amongst the fanbase despite a run to the FA Cup final.

The appointment of Xabi Alonso and a redefined recruitment policy has galvanised the supporters. Stamford Bridge felt alive again during their thrilling 4-3 victory over Brighton. There is plenty of work for Alonso to do on the pitch but things are looking bright.

The only sour note of the window has been the Enzo Fernandez saga. It has been a contentious issue which has left fans divided. Creating a deadline - set for 5pm on August 15 - didn't have the desired impact.

No guarantees were offered that the Argentina midfielder would remain and the uncertainty crept into the new campaign. However, a record of three wins from three matches would suggest that internally the squad have been unaffected.

In Emiliano Martinez, Morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix , Chelsea have signed three players who immediately strengthen their starting XI.

Losing Marc Cucurella was a blow but one of a number of impressive sales. The club succeeded in achieving their high valuation for players surplus to requirements, such as Liam Delap , Nicolas Jackson and Alejandro Garnacho .

Chelsea have proven to be world-class player traders in recent years. The question now will be whether they can deliver world-class results on the pitch.

Coventry had an ambitious summer. They spent big but there has been a clear plan behind it, mixing Premier League experience with younger signings who can grow with the club.

The biggest improvement is the depth available to Frank Lampard. Carl Rushworth has returned permanently after playing such a big role in last season's promotion, while Aurele Amenda adds athleticism at centre-back. Caleb Yirenkyi is an exciting signing in midfield, with Frank Onyeka bringing Premier League experience and Gustavo Hamer adding familiarity and creativity.

Up front, Taiwo Awoniyi gives Coventry a proven Premier League focal point, while Loum Tchaouna and Sidiki Cherif add pace and potential.

Questions remain about whether the new-look attack will produce enough goals, particularly after two defeats without scoring to start the season, but the squad is unquestionably stronger and has far more depth than the one that won promotion.

For a newly promoted side, Coventry have been bold without looking reckless. A very strong window with a serious statement of intent.

In Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Munoz , it is without doubt that Crystal Palace lost two of their best players this summer.

But Palace will see keeping hold of Adam Wharton , Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr as a big win.

Mateta got over transfer heartbreak last January when a move to AC Milan fell through and he may need to coach his team-mate Sarr through the next few months after Liverpool's efforts to sign him didn't come off.

Mateta himself is in the last year of his contract, but are we just four months away from another window where his future is up for speculation?

Sarr's performances from now until January will determine whether Palace's strong stance on him staying was correct.

Palace, as is the norm, have had to try to be clever in the market. Their signings have been sensible rather than sensational.

Axel Disasi , Dwight McNeil , Ben Chilwell and Takehiro Tomiyasu are all very capable Premier League players.

Dario Osorio could be the gem. The 22-year-old comes highly rated and Palace have a habit of unearthing big talents. Honest Ahanor is young but is a good addition at the back.

Time will tell, but Anan Khalaili looks like he has the potential to eventually fill Daniel Munoz's shoes.

Overall, Palace finished the window with better depth than they started, which is crucial for another season with European football.

They've become experts at losing big players and dealing with it. Michael Olise, Eberechi Eze and Marc Guehi have left and Palace have not just survived but thrived.

Palace will be an interesting story. You can't say their business this summer guarantees success. But a late flurry of deals, matched with early considered signings, makes one feel they'll be satisfied with the window.

That's Everton that! But how have they got to a situation where they've halved a strike force that was far from prolific anyway?

Easy to say in hindsight but allowing Beto to go to Fiorentina before a deal for Folarin Balogun was signed and sealed now looks amateur at best. The unsuccessful pivot to Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee when the Balogun deal initially faltered just adds to the feeling of a chaotic and panicked end to the window.

Add to that the sale of their most exciting talent, Iliman Ndiaye . All window, it was emphasised Everton were in a position of strength given he had three years left on his contract. Yet a deal to sell was struck at £65m . Over four times the amount Everton paid two years ago but not the figure that would have made it that bit more palatable for the fans.

Of course Ndiaye was initially off to Spurs for £60m with Richarlison coming the other way for £35m. A fee for the Brazilian that, even taking into account the esteem in which he's held by the blue half of Merseyside, appeared to be on the high side and ultimately was the first of Everton's proposed Deadline Day deals to fall through.

Kenny Tete was another. Fulham weren't letting him go without knowing they definitely had a replacement - a lesson in that, perhaps. So a tumultuous end to a window that has been far from easy when you consider the club's ownership mulling over Nottingham Forest's £40m offer to buy Harrison Armstrong at a time when David Moyes was talking up the need for getting players in.

And Evertonians could do with some positivity. At the moment, they are hurt, embarrassed, angry, frustrated and concerned, when the facts are that it didn't need to be like this.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles, Jack Grealish , Hayden Hackney , Christian Norgaard , Merlin Rohl , Tyrique George and Brennan Johnson have all arrived.

Unfortunately, the positives are more than overshadowed by the fact that the manager has, again, not been given the tools that will give him the best chance of delivering success.

Last season it was the failure to bring in a right-back and a proven striker. This season he has to muddle through until at least January with Thierno Barry as his only recognised front man.

Given the circumstances, it's difficult to see them muster a challenge for Europe - and if that is the case it shouldn't be seen as a failure.

For Fulham, the real proof will be in the eating over the next few months. With Alvaro Arbeloa looking to introduce a new high-pressing, high-tempo approach at Craven Cottage, there will inevitably be a bedding-in period.

But on paper, Fulham have addressed several of the key areas they needed to strengthen.

The biggest requirement was a quality striker and in Gonzalo García , arriving from Real Madrid, they appear to have found one.

His early return is certainly encouraging, scoring twice in his first three games.

The midfield has also been significantly strengthened. Fulham have added two more Real Madrid academy graduates in Cesar Palacios and Manuel Angel , while Shea Charles arrives from Southampton and Hugo Larsson from Eintracht Frankfurt.

That gives Arbeloa considerably more depth and variety in the middle of the pitch, with a mixture of energy, technical quality and flexibility. The biggest question mark remains at the back.

We have already seen Fulham exposed defensively and that is perhaps an inevitable consequence of Arbeloa's philosophy. His centre-backs are being asked to defend higher up the pitch, while the full-backs are encouraged to push even further forward.

That makes the Deadline Day signing of David Affengruber particularly interesting. The Austria international's profile appears well suited to Arbeloa's demands and his ability to defend space could prove valuable in a system that asks so much of its defenders.

Despite losing Harry Wilson and Samuel Chukwueze , Fulham have not signed a winger in this window. That is a surprise and will leave some fans concerned. Palacios - who started on the left wing against Chelsea and Sunderland - is not a specialist winger.

Nonetheless, Fulham's summer business feels ambitious. They have recruited players who fit the manager's vision, rather than just filling gaps in the squad.

If Arbeloa can get the balance right between aggression and defensive security, Fulham have the ingredients to avoid a relegation battle.

Hull were looking to add pace, athleticism and quality to their squad in this window - and they've certainly achieved that.

Eighteen new players have arrived, including six on Deadline Day. Owner Acun Ilicali has played a key role in the recruitment process, convincing prospective signings of the club's huge ambition. And there is a feeling that a patient approach has helped them to land their primary targets on favourable terms.

The club has added strength in depth, with young players targeted who can develop and improve with the club. Although that approach does bring an element of risk, it also offers huge reward if they are successful.

The starting XI has been improved but significantly, the core of the side that helped Hull achieve promotion remains, with an emphasis on retaining that spirit which could be so important to the club's survival hopes in a tough Premier League season.

Ipswich can look back on an extremely busy summer transfer window, with 14 incomings and 18 departures, as one that certainly suggests they have learnt from two years ago.

Approximately £110m was spent in the summer of 2024 to try and help the club remain a Premier League side. That failed, but fast-forward two years and £200m spent in this window, topped up by the Deadline Day signing of Zian Flemming from Burnley, and the club are certainly showing their ambition.

They've added experience, physicality and Premier League know-how, while bringing in players with the potential to grow into major assets for the club.

Julio Enciso has arrived as a record signing, while Abdul Fatawu , Emersonn and Exequiel Palacios add real quality and attacking threat. Sasa Lukic , Issa Diop and Florentino Luis also bring Premier League experience , while Daizen Maeda brings pace and proven pedigree.

What stands out is the depth Ipswich now have across the squad. They haven't simply replaced players - they have strengthened almost every area. It's now down to Gary O'Neil to gel the group together quickly and continue what's been an encouraging start to the new campaign.

All the focus will understandably be on the success story of Leeds' Deadline Day - and how different it feels to 12 months ago when they missed out on Harry Wilson at the last minute - but the most crucial part of their business was done earlier in the summer.

By signing Wilson, Tarik Muharemovic and James Trafford , Daniel Farke has upgraded three key positions. The Leeds manager has been keen to improve the individual quality in his squad and this trio does that. All of them make his starting XI better.

Signing those three would not have been enough though. Leeds had a squad depth issue last season and by signing Nico Elvedi , Michael Zetterer and Melvin Bard, they have begun to properly address that.

The last man through the door, Jean-Matteo Bahoya , is the wild card. The winger provides an X factor and lightning-quick pace that make him a potential game-changing signing. It is up to him now to see if he can deliver on that promise.

If we revisit 12 months down the line and Bahoya is a hit, Leeds' window goes up another level. Regardless, the hierarchy at Leeds have delivered a squad capable of achieving their goal of consolidating their place in the Premier League.

Liverpool have ticked a number of boxes that many will have seen as a priority.

Pace in the wide attacking areas has been addressed with the signings of Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz .

In turn, with Cody Gakpo staying (he was never going to be sold after Liverpool were knocked back in approaches for Yankuba Minteh and Ismaila Sarr ), Andoni Iraola now has four wide options to choose from when you add the emerging talent of Rio Ngumoha to that. He also retains Gakpo as a possible backup to Alexander Isak with Hugo Ekitike still injured.

They've strengthened at the back with Ronald Araujo able to cover both centre-back and right-back. A crucial addition given the injuries to Joe Gomez , Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni . Araujo also approaches the game in a way that contrasts yet complements that of Jeremy Jacquet , whose deal was sorted in the winter window before signing this summer, and who already looks the part as a Liverpool centre-half.

On the flip side, when one of the priorities was to fill the position vacated by Mohamed Salah , Liverpool have not been able to bring in a naturally right-sided winger even though Barcola, Gakpo, Ngumoha and Munoz have all played out there at various points in their career.

I agree with those who feel that at least another quality full-back option and a holding midfielder would have made a massive difference to this squad's potential.

Barcola brings undoubted star quality. Munoz looks like he has the mentality to thrive, while Jacquet's style, coupled with Araujo's attitude, already resonates with the fans. So to deem this window a failure would be wrong.

The average age of Liverpool's first-team signings over the last two summer windows is around 22, which is another positive.

And in another nod to the future, they've been able to secure deals for two 18-year-olds in Lucca Brughmans and Djylian N'Guessan, who will join up properly in time for the start of next season.

At the same time, when the squad is not as well-rounded as it could be, there is an argument to say it could have been better.

It sounds a bit ridiculous to score Man City highly, given they had to allow Rodri , the best player at the World Cup, to leave for Barcelona. However, just as the fans were beginning to get restless, City managed to pull a couple of big-money irons from the dying embers of the transfer window.

Enzo Fernandez made all the headlines on a dramatic Deadline Day that saw them smash their transfer record for the second time this summer. He'll potentially partner Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi in a new-look £300m midfield that will be the envy of many around Europe.

Those close to the club are adamant the squad is in better shape now than it was at the start of last season, with the money received for Savio , Omar Marmoush , Nico Gonzalez , Tijjani Reijnders , Nathan Ake and James Trafford allowing them to also add Iliman Ndiaye and Allan to their attacking options.

Enzo Maresca has the tools he wanted for his revolution - time to see if it'll be enough to fight for the title.

Some may be surprised by me giving Manchester United a relatively high score in the transfer market - but let me explain my thought process.

United went into the window needing to rebuild their midfield. That was their priority, and three signings later, with around £155m spent, they have done that.

Andrey Santos , Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba will balance United's midfield alongside Kobbie Mainoo, and the combinations Michael Carrick now has at his disposal for the competitions they will compete in this season give room for optimism.

Yes, they did not get a left-back and it is clear they lack depth in that position - however, it is easy to forget they have players who can play in that position. Noussair Mazraoui deputised there well for Morocco in this summer's World Cup, while Diogo Dalot can also feature there.

Ultimately, United did not see the departures they perhaps imagined at the beginning of the window. Joshua Zirkzee , Manuel Ugarte and Marcus Rashford staying limited their ability to strengthen other positions.

However, if Rashford continues to build on his promising performances at the start of the season, he could be like a new signing for Carrick.

The summer transformation is complete at Newcastle, with Matias Fernandez-Pardo on Deadline Day becoming their eighth signing.

Of the eight, Lukas Hornicek , Amar Dedic , Nico Gonzalez and Fernandez-Pardo come into the strongest XI, but there's still so much headroom to improve for the likes of Sean Steur , Aladji Bamba , Bazoumana Toure and Ewan Jaouen , who are all very young and raw.

Newcastle have spent £262m this summer, having raked in £245m for Sandro Tonali , Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon .

They've beefed up the squad and made it youthful. But the last two signings of Gonzalez and Fernandez-Pardo for a combined £101m feel the most important. And the most ambitious.

For a window that at one stage looked as though it would be a disaster after a couple of early hijacks, Newcastle have turned the ship around.

And the early displays of Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa (who arrived for a combined £110m last summer) make the team feel like they have two more new signings.

A solid first window for new boss Oliver Glasner .

He wanted a physical No 9 with a high upside - he got that in Liam Delap . He wanted a starting-calibre wing-back - he got that by reuniting with Daniel Munoz . Ousmane Diomande was a Glasner target and the manager's also working again with Xaver Schlager after their time together at Wolfsburg.

The one slight on their summer business is failing to replace Elliot Anderson with a young, dynamic, forward-thinking midfielder. They did, however, get good money from Man City.

Sunderland left it until the dying moments of Deadline Day to add the winger that they had wanted all window.

They didn't originally want Malick Fofana , but they worked their way down the list until Fofana was the best option with less than 24 hours to go.

But the Lyon winger made it difficult for them, and a crazy tug-of-war between themselves and Crystal Palace ensued at Lyon airport.

It took Sunderland owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus stepping in, throwing more money at the situation, and getting the deal over the line.

Fofana gets in Sunderland's starting XI - he has to for all that hassle getting the deal done.

So too does big summer signing Dayann Methalie . But the key for Sunderland this window has been holding onto their big-hitters like Granit Xhaka , Brian Brobbey and Noah Sadiki .

In terms of commitment to spending, it's 10/10. Tottenham kept their promise to spend big. But for the individuals, the jury is out at the moment, and Spurs are one of many clubs that have perhaps overpaid. So as it stands, a seven.

It's been a window unlike any I can remember. Spurs came out of the blocks with eye-opening signings, such as beating Manchester United to Mateus Fernandes and signing a player in Sandro Tonali that many would have thought out of their reach.

Roberto De Zerbi has been given the keys to reshape the Tottenham squad. A prime example is spending around £50m on Jan Paul van Hecke , who had only one year on his contract. That is something you would never expect from Spurs.

While the defence and midfield have been worked on, the clear issue last season was a lack of quality in the forward areas. The year-long pursuit of Savio finally came to a conclusion and he was joined by Omar Marmoush to the delight of the fans.

De Zerbi then told Sky Sports News he wanted one more big signing. That was believed to be Cody Gakpo - but City joined the race and it was clear that, if he were to leave, he would be going to Manchester.

After a disappointing defeat to Newcastle, Spurs fans woke up to another 'bomba', with a fee agreed with Everton for Iliman Ndiaye , and Richarlison going the other way. This is a player who would have got bums off seats. But on Monday, Ndiaye chose City and Richarlison publicly criticised the club.

Spurs then contacted rivals Chelsea for Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo . Mudryk's arrival signifies the board and scouting department have given De Zerbi full backing.

Spurs and Chelsea do not do business. Times are changing, finances are changing, board members change. Mudryk is a big risk - he hasn't played competitive football in nearly two years.

But if De Zerbi can get the best out of him, it could prove to be a shrewd signing. Chelsea's insistence of a high loan-to-buy fee shows they haven't totally given up on Mudryk either.

articles.title: Notre Dame Unveils Helmet Decal Honoring Lou Holtz in New Video Ahead of 2026 CFB Opener
articles.summary: Notre Dame will honor legendary coach Lou Holtz by wearing a special helmet decal during the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Notre Dame will honor legendary coach Lou Holtz by wearing a special helmet decal during the 2026 college football season.

The Fighting Irish shared a video Wednesday showing a decal made in honor of Holtz, who died in March at age 89.

USC HC Claps Back at Attendance Criticism

Holtz won 100 games with Notre Dame while coaching the program from 1986 to 1996, a stretch that included a run to the 1988 national championship. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2008.

The Fighting Irish are set to open the season while wearing the new decals Sunday against visiting Wisconsin.

William & Mary, where Holtz began his head coaching career in 1969, will honor the late coach the day prior during their home opener against Delaware State.

articles.title: Summer transfers 2026: All to know as Premier League signings break records
articles.summary: Premier League breaks its own record as four of its 11 most expensive signings have arrived this transfer window.
articles.body:
The English Premier League displayed its financial power once again by smashing the summer transfer window record for the amount spent by its clubs on new players.

It had only set the previous record last year.

The spree continued deep into the final hours of the window, which shut on Tuesday , with several big-money deals completed before the 11pm (22:00 GMT) deadline for signings by English clubs.

Approximately 38 percent of the Premier League deals were made between the clubs from within that competition, up from 30 percent last year’s summer transfer window.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at major takeaways from the 2026-27 transfer window:

How much did Premier League clubs spend for the 2026-27 season?

A total of 3.46 billion pounds ($4.67bn) was dished out by England’s top-flight clubs, with 475 million pounds ($640.1m) being spent on deadline day itself, up from 391 million pounds ($526.7m) on the same day last year.

During the last summer transfer window, the combined spending of the league’s 20 clubs breached the 3 billion pounds ($4.05bn) barrier for the first time, while this year’s figure dwarfed the 1.13 billion pounds ($1.52bn) spent five years ago.

What were the most expensive Premier League and La Liga signings?

Manchester City topped the list when they spent 125 million pounds ($168.7m) on signing Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea.

He’s the first player to be transferred twice for figures upwards of 100 million pounds ($134.7m), and his deal equalled the amount spent on Aleksander Isak when he moved from Newcastle United to Liverpool during the last summer transfer window.

Liverpool paid a close second 123 million pounds ($166m) to sign France forward Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

Chelsea followed with 117 million pounds ($158m) spent on bringing England international Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa to Stamford Bridge, while Manchester City dished out 116 million pounds ($156.6m) for midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest.

Which clubs spent the most money on summer transfers?

Manchester City’s signing of Fernandez capped the whopping 458 million pounds ($618.2m) spent as new manager Enzo Maresca assembled his first squad, which includes Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi for 86 million pounds ($116.2m).

It was a new Premier League record that surpassed the 415 million pounds (560.3m) paid by Liverpool last year.

Chelsea also spent heavily, shelling out 349 million pounds ($471.1m) to back new boss Xabi Alonso.

Tottenham splashed out 303 million pounds ($409m) as they rebuild after two successive seasons close to being relegated.

Promoted trio Ipswich, Coventry City and Hull City spent more than a combined 400 million pounds ($539.9m) to prepare themselves for life in the top flight.

Sunderland landed highly rated Belgian winger Malick Fofana, 21, from Olympique Lyonnais in a reported 30 million pounds ($40.5m) deal after beating Crystal Palace to his signature.

Tottenham Hotspur also broke their club transfer record to sign Sandro Tonali from Newcastle United in a deal that could reach 100 million pounds ($134.9m).

Why did Julian Alvarez, Folarin Balogun and Lamine Camara fail to join a new club?

Some deals failed to go through on deadline day.

British media reported that Everton’s move for Folarin Balogun collapsed after the US striker decided against proceeding with the transfer, while Senegal midfielder Lamine Camara remained at Monaco after his reported 47.1 million pounds ($63.5m) move to Chelsea fell through.

Julian Alvarez’s dream of playing for Barcelona never materialised after Atletico held onto him despite strong interest from Barcelona and Arsenal.

Atletico chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin made his feelings quite clear about ⁠⁠Barcelona last week and ⁠⁠said Alvarez would never be sold to them.

“There has not been, and there will not be any negotiation with them [Barcelona] regarding Alvarez’s transfer,” Atletico’s board of directors said in the statement.

“Atletico de Madrid is open to standard transfer market negotiations when conducted in a professional, ethical and respectful manner,” the statement added.

articles.title: Tenaglia cotiza al alza
articles.standfirst: El argentino atraviesa el mejor momento de su carrera y su nivel en estos tres partidos ha sido excelso.
articles.summary: El argentino atraviesa el mejor momento de su carrera y su nivel en estos tres partidos ha sido excelso.
articles.body: Hace tiempo que Nahuel Tenaglia no es un futbolista más en Mendizorroza. El defensa argentino representa todos los valores que reúnen las leyendas del conjunto babazorro y cada partido que suma con la elástica albiazul dignifica como pocos el privilegio de defender los colores albiazules. En una entrevista concedida a MARCA este verano, reconocía que la pasada temporada fue “la mejor campaña” de su carrera, pero este curso quiere mejorarla y el inicio de curso avala esta posibilidad. El defensa de Saladillo fue el autor del primer gol de la presente temporada en el fútbol español con un cabezazo que venía precedido de una recuperación suya. Tenaglia abrió la lata ante el Getafe para completar una gran actuación defensiva que ha mantenido en las dos siguientes jornadas. Estuvo a un buen nivel en la visita a Butarque y volvió a sobresalir el pasado viernes en el segundo encuentro del curso en Mendizorroza con otro triunfo de mucho valor ante el Villarreal. Tenaglia comenzó el encuentro como central, pero pronto pasó a ocupar el lateral derecho tras el cambio de dibujo de Quique Sánchez Flores. Tuvo más protagonismo en ataque acompañando a Ángel Pérez en sus ataques y en la segunda mitad, con el marcador a favor y el ‘Submarino’ acumulando jugadores ofensivos en busca de la igualada, el argentino estuvo sobresaliente en varias acciones decisivas que evitaron el gol que hubiese costado dos puntos al Alavés. A sus 30 años, el ex de Talleres se encuentra en el mejor momento de su carrera. Tanto en lo físico como en lo anímico. Ha perdido peso, se le ve más veloz y las lesiones le respetan. Acumula casi dos años sin pasar por la enfermería. Tiempo en el que ha formado parte de todas las convocatorias, exceptuando dos de ellas por sanción. Una garantía de rendimiento, que además casa a la perfección con el sentimiento babazorro y que está preparado para subir aún más la nota que sacó el año pasado.

articles.title: Winners and Losers From the 2026 Summer Transfer Window
articles.summary: The 2026 summer transfer window has finally shut for Europe's top leagues, either providing a huge wave of relief or even more reason to despair.
articles.body:
The 2026 summer transfer window has finally shut for Europe's top leagues, either providing a huge wave of relief or even more reason to despair.

Deadline day was typically chaotic—just ask Everton. While some deals were completed at the very last second, some players and clubs were left wondering why they had wasted their precious time.

Ahead, Calum Rogers, Nick Akerman and Leo Collis have taken a look at the winners and losers from the whole of the signing period.

Got any to add? Leave your winners and losers in the comments.

Typically it would be difficult to call a team that has lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in a single transfer window a winner, but Manchester City have immediately rebuilt their midfield with three of the top players on the market.

Signing one of Elliot Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez would've been a necessary response to the departure of two club legends in the same position. Adding two would have raised hopes that City may be strong enough to reclaim the Premier League crown this season. In acquiring all three, they have provided manager Enzo Maresca with little excuse but to turn this team into title challengers immediately.

When you add in that City also signed Iliman Ndiaye and received over $250 million for backups in Savio, Nico Gonzalez, Tijjani Reijnders and Omar Marmoush, it's hard to envision how this summer could've gone much better for them.

Yes, there are still some question marks in the back four, particularly at right-back. But City have the best striker in the league in Erling Haaland, arguably the two best wingers from last season in Antoine Semenyo and Jeremy Doku, and now a midfield that is once again stacked with talent.

I picked Arsenal to win the league prior to the season , but City might have just done enough to make it back to the summit again.

It must be pretty disheartening to miss your dream move as a footballer. We all know Julian Alvarez was desperate to go to Barcelona. However, he resides at possibly one of the two clubs that would be unwilling to sanction that.

Atletico Madrid have every right not to significantly strengthen their rivals. Alvarez isn't a goal machine, but he is extremely effective on the ball, a hard worker and capable of consistently providing match-winning moments. To hand that over to the defending champions would be nothing short of unfathomable for Atleti.

Arsenal's interest represented a good opportunity for the Rojiblancos, who likely would have cashed in if the player wanted to head back to England. He clearly didn't, though. It's interesting that he decided to stick around in Spain. Alvarez has previous for Man City, likely the closest challenger to Arsenal's title defence, so perhaps he didn't want to jeopardise his reputation there. But in this situation, nobody wins.

Alvarez is back in training, after being 'ill', at a club he doesn't want to play for. Barca don't have their man. Arsenal failed to strengthen their attack, with all eggs in the Alvarez basket until the last couple of days of the window.

Will things change in January? Should he have used Arsenal as a stepping stone to get to the Camp Nou? So many questions unanswered after months of the window being open is a disaster for the player.

It's rare that Real Madrid would come out of any transfer window as anything other than winners. But in the summer of 2026, Los Blancos really nailed their business.

They avoided losing one of their best players in Vinicius Junior by finally getting him to sign a new contract. Arsenal were a legitimate threat at one point, but the Brazilian put pen to paper to keep him at the Santiago Bernabeu until 2032.

Real also made some shrewd free-agent pickups, getting Ibrahima Konate after he left Liverpool and grabbing Bernardo Silva following his Manchester City departure.

The signing of Marc Cucurella, a World Cup-winning left-back and one of the best in his position, was a fine move for a not-so-ridiculous outlay. Meanwhile, snagging Denzel Dumfries on the cheap from Internazionale adds depth to the right-back position and provides competition for Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Then there's Yan Diomande. Real Madrid won the race for the Ivory Coast starlet's signature, fending off Paris Saint-Germain and Liverpool, among others. Players typically don't say no when the La Liga giants come calling, but it was still a statement of superiority that they secured a player who could be a future Ballon d'Or contender. He will bring magic to Madrid for the next decade or so.

All in all, Real Madrid reinforced an already top-quality squad with world-class talent without dropping obscene amounts of cash—relatively speaking. It doesn't get much better than that.

Beto never scored more than 10 goals in a Premier League season in three years with Everton. So, when his departure for Fiorentina was confirmed while Everton looked set to bring in a replacement, there was little concern that the 28-year-old would be missed on Merseyside.

However, after a move for Monaco's Folarin Balogun was called off, revived and then called off again (with a brief swoop for Manchester United flop Joshua Zirkzee also failing), Everton fans could be forgiven for recreating the Wolverine meme with pictures of their now-former No. 9.

The Toffees are left with only Thierno Barry as a recognized striker until January at least, unless they can find someone they like on the free-agent market (Jamie Vardy, anyone?).

The bright side of this may be that the 23-year-old Barry will have all the opportunity in the world to build on a 2025/26 campaign that saw him register eight league goals. But even in the most optimistic scenario for Barry's development, Tuesday's failure has effectively torched any hope of a successful first half of the season for Everton.

They will now be relying on Barry to both display rapid improvement and stay healthy, with winger Brennan Johnson the most likely alternative if the 6'5" Frenchman does miss time. But this failure will also see Everton enter the winter window with every other club knowing they're desperate for a striker, which will make it almost impossible to find value in what is already a difficult market.

For a team that previously had justifiable ambitions of a top-half finish this season, deadline day couldn't have gone much worse.

For Luke Shaw to be Manchester United's uncontested left-back in 2026 is quite astonishing. The 31-year-old moved to Old Trafford in 2014. In that time, he's suffered a horrific injury, constant fitness issues, and questioning about his suitability for a club of United's size. Granted, Shaw put together arguably his best season last time out, but it almost feels negligent that he has no real competition and a long campaign, including European football, ahead.

United will say Patrick Dorgu can play at left-back. They'll mention Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui, and maybe even new midfield signing Carlos Baleba. Youngster Harry Amass, who United nearly let leave this week, is also there. None of these are ideal solutions to the problem that really should have been solved by going for Newcastle's Lewis Hall.

If this was Manchester City, they would have paid what was needed to get it done, rather than waiting until next year, when competition for the Englishman is likely to be fierce. United are hamstrung by previous failures in the market and no longer have the capital to act so forcefully.

That's a huge win for Shaw, whose lack of attacking quality quietly hampers a side that rarely gets impactful offensive contributions from its full-backs.

Shaw hasn't had more than two assists in a Premier League season since 2021-22. Considering Ipswich's wingers ran through him like he wasn't there during United's recent 5-2 win, he's somewhat lucky to still have such an easy route into Michael Carrick's first team.

Engineering your way out of a football club doesn't always work. If Julian Alvarez proved that in Spain, Ismaïla Sarr and Richarlison were left looking equally as silly in England.

Let's start with Sarr. The Crystal Palace winger had already been denied a move to Galatasaray before Liverpool started sniffing around.

The Senegal international pulled the "get me out of here" lever, deleting any mention of his current club from his Instagram profile. But, with the Reds unable to agree a reasonable fee with the Eagles, the 28-year-old is staying put.

Now, Sarr either has to return to the training pitch with his tail between his legs and apologize to his teammates and coaches, or he goes on strike, potentially courting clubs in Saudi Arabia where the transfer window is still open.

Then we have Richarlison. While his situation wasn't helped by a shambolic end to the window for Tottenham Hotspur and Everton, his statement on social media calling for "respect" from the club as he tried to return to the Toffees arguably didn't make things any easier.

Now, with a deal failing to come to fruition, he's left in an awkward predicament with Tottenham, despite stating that he remains "at the club's disposal."

Both players are now in serious danger of being left out of matchday squads for the next four months or so, with relief possibly arriving when the winter window opens.

articles.title: Diomande: "Con Vinicius y Mbappé no te queda otra que subir tu nivel"
articles.standfirst: El flamante fichaje madridista repasa su vertiginoso camino, del asfalto de Abiyán al Bernabéu, en su primera entrevista como deportista de Red Bull
articles.summary: El flamante fichaje madridista repasa su vertiginoso camino, del asfalto de Abiyán al Bernabéu, en su primera entrevista como deportista de Red Bull
articles.body: Yan Diomande, flamante fichaje del Real Madrid y ya nuevo atleta de Red Bull, repasó en una entrevista de presentación con la marca su fulgurante trayectoria, desde las calles de Abiyán hasta el vestuario blanco. El marfileño arrancó recordando unos orígenes humildes que siguen marcando su manera de entender el fútbol. "Crecer en Abiyán significaba que el fútbol lo era todo. Jugábamos en cualquier superficie que encontrábamos, sin botas de verdad ni un campo apropiado, solo por amor al fútbol", rememoró. "Esa hambre y esa alegría nunca me abandonaron; siguen siendo la base de cómo juego hoy". El sueño de dedicarse a esto, confiesa, tardó en tomar forma real. Fue en Estados Unidos, adonde emigró con apenas 15 años y sin hablar inglés, donde empezó a vislumbrar un futuro profesional. "Siempre fue el sueño, pero empezó a parecer real cuando estaba en la DME Academy de Florida y los ojeadores europeos comenzaron a fijarse en mí", explicó. Aquella adaptación, sin embargo, no fue sencilla: "Fue difícil, al principio no podía comunicarme con nadie y todo era diferente. Pero el fútbol era mi idioma, y mis compañeros me ayudaron a encontrar mi sitio dentro y fuera del campo". Su explosión definitiva llegó en el RB Leipzig, la etapa de la que guarda su logro más preciado. "Ganar el premio al Mejor Rookie de la Bundesliga en mi primera temporada completa. Fue la prueba de que todos los sacrificios que mi familia y yo hicimos merecieron la pena", destacó. Aquel curso, subraya, resultó determinante para dar el salto al Madrid. "El Leipzig me enseñó a competir al más alto nivel semana tras semana, y el cuerpo técnico me exigió mejorar cada detalle de mi juego. Esa temporada me dio la confianza y la mentalidad que voy a necesitar en el Real Madrid". Precisamente sobre lo que significa vestir de blanco, el atacante no ocultó la emoción. "Es cumplir un sueño de infancia, es todo por lo que he trabajado", afirmó. "Estoy deseando escribir mi capítulo en este club y contribuir a sus éxitos". Un reto que afronta después de haber vivido su primer Mundial con Costa de Marfil, una experiencia de la que extrajo valiosas lecciones. "Representar a mi país ante el mundo me enseñó que el escenario más grande exige la mayor serenidad: tienes que confiar en tu preparación. Y fuera del campo, compartir esa experiencia con mi país y mi familia es algo que llevaré siempre conmigo". Ya instalado en Valdebebas, Diomande se declara maravillado por el nivel de sus nuevos compañeros, con Vinicius y Mbappé a la cabeza. "Es increíble. En cada sesión el listón está tan alto que no te queda otra que elevar tu propio nivel", reconoció. "Aprendes algo solo con ver cómo se mueven, cómo piensan y cómo se preparan cada día". Un aprendizaje diario que el marfileño, a sus 19 años, aspira a exprimir al máximo en su nueva etapa. Lejos de los focos, el joven extremo se define como una persona tranquila y muy apegada a sus raíces, un ancla que le mantiene con los pies en la tierra pese al vértigo de los últimos meses. "Soy bastante tranquilo. Me encanta pasar tiempo con mi familia y mis amigos, escuchar música y llamar a casa, a Abiyán", relató. "Mantener esa conexión con el lugar del que vengo me mantiene centrado". Una humildad que acompaña a la que ya es la mayor promesa del nuevo Madrid.
